To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Financial integration causes boom-bust cycles because moral hazard makes entrepreneurs more risk averse and less willing to invest.” The paper is organized as follows: Section 2 describes the model.

(i) in a setting with risky entrepreneurial activity and moral hazard, financial integration can cause boom-bust cycles of capital flows, output, and consumption; and (ii) these cycles are caused by the interaction of the moral hazard problem and the fact that entrepreneurs have to borrow to finance their projects.

(i) moral hazard is the key mechanism through which capital flow cycles arise in a world economy, and (ii) the moral hazard channel is the main channel through which capital flow volatility is transmitted to output and consumption volatility in an economy.
